findings.title: Exit code 4 changed meaning: was 'recreate required', now 'feature disabled'
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3 and 4 is now reused for FEATURE_DISABLED. Any existing automation/pipeline written against the previously released behaviour that treats exit code 4 as 'recreate upgrade required' will now silently interpret a 'feature not enabled' failure as a recreate signal (and vice versa, a real recreate requirement returns 3 which such scripts likely treat as unexpected). If backwards compatibility matters, pick an unused code (e.g. 5) for FEATURE_DISABLED instead of recycling 4, and call out the change in the release notes.

findings.title: Feature-disabled path only tested for 'metadata', exit code not asserted
findings.body: testFeatureNotEnabled only exercises the `metadata` subcommand and asserts the error text; it does not assert the new exit code (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) nor cover the `check` subcommand, which has the same new guard. Since the documented contract is the exit code (docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc lists code 4), a regression in the exit code or in the `check` guard would go unnoticed.
